adinkrahene.name: Adinkrahene
adinkrahene.description: Chief of the Adinkra symbols; symbol of greatness, charisma and leadership. Said to have inspired the design of the other Adinkra symbols.

akoben.name: Akoben
akoben.description: Symbol of vigilance and wariness. Akoben is a war horn used to rally troops to battle — a call to action and readiness.
akoben.proverb: The horn that calls the warriors to duty.

akofena.name: Akofena
akofena.description: Symbol of courage, valor and heroism. Crossed state swords used in oath-swearing and as emblems of legitimate state authority.
akofena.proverb: The sword of war — courage in the service of a just cause.

akoko-nan.name: Akoko Nan
akoko-nan.description: Symbol of mercy, nurturing and firm-but-fair parenting. The hen may tread on her chicks, but she does not kill them.
akoko-nan.proverb: Akoko nan tia ba na enkum ba — 'the hen's foot steps on the chick but does not crush it'.

akoma-ntoso.name: Akoma Ntoso
akoma-ntoso.description: Symbol of understanding and agreement — 'linked hearts'. Represents the harmony of a community in accord.

akoma.name: Akoma
akoma.description: Symbol of patience, love, endurance, goodwill, faithfulness and tolerance — literally, 'the heart'. 'Take heart' is a common Akan expression of forbearance.
akoma.proverb: Nya akoma — 'have a heart; be patient'.

ananse-ntontan.name: Ananse Ntontan
ananse-ntontan.description: The spider's web — symbol of wisdom, creativity and the complexities of life. Named after Kwaku Ananse, the legendary spider-trickster of Akan folklore.
ananse-ntontan.proverb: The web of the wise spider catches everything.

asase-ye-duru.name: Asase Ye Duru
asase-ye-duru.description: 'The Earth has weight' — symbol of the divinity of Mother Earth, her power to sustain life, and the importance of the land to the people who live on it.
asase-ye-duru.proverb: Asase ye duru sen po — 'the Earth is heavier than the sea'.

aya.name: Aya
aya.description: The fern — symbol of endurance, resourcefulness, defiance and independence. One who wears Aya says, 'I have endured hardships and outlasted my adversaries.'
aya.proverb: I am not afraid of you; I can thrive where little else does.

bese-saka.name: Bese Saka
bese-saka.description: 'A sack of cola nuts' — symbol of affluence, plenty, abundance and togetherness. Cola nuts were historically an important cash crop and ceremonial gift in Akan society.
bese-saka.proverb: Where many cola nuts are gathered, many hands have worked.

bi-nka-bi.name: Bi Nka Bi
bi-nka-bi.description: 'No one should bite another' — symbol of peace, harmony and the avoidance of conflict, provocation and strife.
bi-nka-bi.proverb: Bi nka bi — 'do not bite one another'.

boa-me-na-me-mmoa-wo.name: Boa Me Na Me Mmoa Wo
boa-me-na-me-mmoa-wo.description: 'Help me and let me help you' — symbol of cooperation and interdependence. A reminder that community is built on mutual aid.
boa-me-na-me-mmoa-wo.proverb: Boa me na me mmoa wo — 'help me so that I may help you'.

dame-dame.name: Dame Dame
dame-dame.description: Named after the board game 'dame-dame' (similar to draughts/checkers) — symbol of intelligence, strategy and ingenuity.
dame-dame.proverb: The wise move is planned many steps ahead.

denkyem.name: Denkyem
denkyem.description: The crocodile — symbol of adaptability and cleverness. It lives in water yet breathes air, demonstrating the ability to thrive in changing environments.
denkyem.proverb: Denkyem da nsu mu nanso ohome mframa — 'the crocodile lives in water yet breathes air'.

duafe.name: Duafe
duafe.description: The wooden comb — symbol of beauty, cleanliness, love and feminine qualities. Prized as a personal, carefully-crafted tool of grooming.
duafe.proverb: Duafe — that which makes one beautiful.

dwennimmen.name: Dwennimmen
dwennimmen.description: 'Ram's horns' — symbol of humility together with strength. Even the strong should be humble; the ram is powerful but submits to slaughter without fighting back.

eban.name: Eban
eban.description: 'Fence' — symbol of love, safety and security. The home, fenced by love, is the safest place.
eban.proverb: The fence of love guards the home.

epa.name: Epa
epa.description: Handcuffs — symbol of law, justice and captivity. A reminder that the law binds both the wrongdoer and the one who enforces it.
epa.proverb: Onii a ɔde epa no, ɔno ara na epa no kyere no — 'he who puts the handcuffs on, the handcuffs also hold'.

ese-ne-tekrema.name: Ese Ne Tekrema
ese-ne-tekrema.description: 'The teeth and the tongue' — symbol of friendship and interdependence. Even the closest companions quarrel, but they cannot do without one another.
ese-ne-tekrema.proverb: Ese ne tekrema — teeth and tongue must work together.

fawohodie.name: Fawohodie
fawohodie.description: 'Independence' — symbol of freedom and emancipation. Expresses a longing and a right to self-determination.
fawohodie.proverb: Fawohodie ene obre na enam — 'independence comes with responsibilities'.

fihankra.name: Fihankra
fihankra.description: The traditional Akan compound house — symbol of security, safety and solidarity. The compound encloses a family and keeps them safe together.
fihankra.proverb: A house with many rooms still has one roof.

fofo.name: Fofo
fofo.description: The seeds of the fofo plant that stick to passing cloth — symbol of a warning against jealousy and covetousness. 'What fofo wants, fofo gets.'
fofo.proverb: De fofo pe ne se gyinantwi aba ho — 'what fofo wants, it clings to'.

funtunfunefu-denkyemfunefu.name: Funtunfunefu Denkyemfunefu
funtunfunefu-denkyemfunefu.description: 'Siamese crocodiles' — symbol of democracy and unity in diversity. Two crocodiles share a single stomach yet fight over food, a warning against selfish division.
funtunfunefu-denkyemfunefu.proverb: We share one stomach, yet we fight when we eat.

gye-nyame.name: Gye Nyame
gye-nyame.description: 'Except for God' — symbol of the supremacy and omnipotence of God. The most widely recognized Adinkra symbol.
gye-nyame.proverb: Gye Nyame — 'except for God'; no one has seen the beginning or end of creation.

hwe-mu-dua.name: Hwe Mu Dua
hwe-mu-dua.description: 'Measuring stick' — symbol of examination, quality control and the pursuit of the best possible standard.

hye-won-hye.name: Hye Won Hye
hye-won-hye.description: 'That which does not burn' — symbol of imperishability, toughness and endurance. Reflects the idea that some things cannot be destroyed, no matter what.
hye-won-hye.proverb: Hye won hye — 'that which burns not'.

kete-pa.name: Kete Pa
kete-pa.description: 'A good bed' — symbol of a good marriage. A well-made bed is an image of a stable, loving union.
kete-pa.proverb: A good bed makes a peaceful home.

kintinkantan.name: Kintinkantan
kintinkantan.description: 'Puffed-up extravagance' — symbol against arrogance, presumption and vanity. A reminder not to be proud or boastful of wealth and position.
kintinkantan.proverb: Do not puff yourself up; humility outlives pride.

kwatakye-atiko.name: Kwatakye Atiko
kwatakye-atiko.description: The hairstyle worn by Kwatakye, a legendary war captain — symbol of bravery and valor in war.
kwatakye-atiko.proverb: The brave wear their courage like a crown.

mate-masie.name: Mate Masie
mate-masie.description: 'What I hear, I keep' — symbol of wisdom, knowledge and prudence. Represents the value of listening well and retaining what is taught.
mate-masie.proverb: Mate masie — 'I have heard and kept it'.

me-ware-wo.name: Me Ware Wo
me-ware-wo.description: 'I shall marry you' — symbol of commitment, perseverance and the bond of marriage.
me-ware-wo.proverb: Me ware wo — 'I will marry you', spoken as a lifelong promise.

mframadan.name: Mframadan
mframadan.description: 'Wind-resistant house' — symbol of fortitude, preparedness and the ability to withstand hardship. A house built to weather any storm.
mframadan.proverb: A house that stands in the wind stands forever.

mmere-dane.name: Mmere Dane
mmere-dane.description: 'Time changes' — symbol of change and the dynamics of life. A reminder that nothing remains the same.

mmusuyidee.name: Mmusuyidee
mmusuyidee.description: 'That which removes bad luck' — symbol of good fortune, spiritual sanctity and the sanctification of the self and one's space.
mmusuyidee.proverb: Let evil pass away and let the good remain.

mpatapo.name: Mpatapo
mpatapo.description: 'Knot of pacification / reconciliation' — symbol of peacemaking after strife, binding disputing parties back together.
mpatapo.proverb: A quarrel resolved is a knot retied stronger.

mpuannum.name: Mpuannum
mpuannum.description: 'Five tufts of hair' — a hairstyle associated with priestly office, symbol of loyalty, adroitness and sacred duty.
mpuannum.proverb: The priest is known by his crown of five tufts.

nea-onnim-no-sua-a-ohu.name: Nea Onnim No Sua A Ohu
nea-onnim-no-sua-a-ohu.description: 'He who does not know can know from learning' — symbol of the lifelong pursuit of knowledge. There is no shame in ignorance, only in refusing to learn.
nea-onnim-no-sua-a-ohu.proverb: Nea onnim no sua a, ohu — 'one who does not know becomes knowledgeable by learning'.

nea-ope-se-obedi-hene.name: Nea Ope Se Obedi Hene
nea-ope-se-obedi-hene.description: 'He who wants to be king' — symbol of service and the idea that true leadership is servitude to one's people.
nea-ope-se-obedi-hene.proverb: He who would be chief must first serve.

nkonsonkonson.name: Nkonsonkonson
nkonsonkonson.description: 'Chain link' — symbol of unity, human relations and the inseparable bond of community. We are linked in life and in death.
nkonsonkonson.proverb: A single chain is made of many links.

nkyimkyim.name: Nkyimkyim
nkyimkyim.description: 'Twisted pattern' — symbol of initiative, dynamism and versatility. Life's journey is winding; one must adapt.
nkyimkyim.proverb: The road of life is never a straight line.

nkyimu.name: Nkyimu
nkyimu.description: 'Crossed divisions' — symbol of skillfulness and precision. Refers to the cross-shaped preparatory markings made on cloth before stamping Adinkra symbols.
nkyimu.proverb: Precise work requires a steady hand.

nsaa.name: Nsaa
nsaa.description: A type of rare, hand-woven blanket — symbol of excellence, genuineness and authenticity. 'One who does not know real nsaa buys an imitation.'
nsaa.proverb: Nea onnim nsaa oto n'ago — 'he who does not know real nsaa buys the imitation'.

nsoromma.name: Nsoromma
nsoromma.description: 'Child of the heavens' — the star. Symbol of guardianship and a reminder that we are all dependents of a higher providence.
nsoromma.proverb: We are all children of the sky.

nyame-biribi-wo-soro.name: Nyame Biribi Wo Soro
nyame-biribi-wo-soro.description: 'God is in the heavens' — symbol of hope and the assurance that God will provide.
nyame-biribi-wo-soro.proverb: Nyame biribi wo soro, ma embeka me nsa — 'God, there is something in the heavens; let it reach me'.

nyame-dua.name: Nyame Dua
nyame-dua.description: 'Tree of God' / altar of God — symbol of God's presence, protection and the sacred. Traditionally a three-forked post placed at the entrance of a home.
nyame-dua.proverb: Wherever the Nyame Dua stands, God is acknowledged.

nyame-nnwu-na-mawu.name: Nyame Nnwu Na Mawu
nyame-nnwu-na-mawu.description: 'God never dies, therefore I cannot die' — symbol of the immortality of the human soul, grounded in the everlasting nature of God.
nyame-nnwu-na-mawu.proverb: Nyame nnwu na mawu — 'God does not die, so I shall not die'.

nyame-nti.name: Nyame Nti
nyame-nti.description: 'By God's grace' / 'because of God' — symbol of faith and trust in the divine.
nyame-nti.proverb: Nyame nti mennwe wira — 'by God's grace, I do not eat chaff'.

nyame-ye-ohene.name: Nyame Ye Ohene
nyame-ye-ohene.description: 'God is King' — symbol of the majesty and supremacy of God above all earthly rulers.
nyame-ye-ohene.proverb: Nyame ye ohene — 'God is the King'.

nyansapo.name: Nyansapo
nyansapo.description: 'The wisdom knot' — symbol of wisdom, ingenuity, intelligence and patience. 'A wise person has the capacity to choose the best means to attain a goal.'
nyansapo.proverb: Nyansapo wosane no badwemma — 'only the wise can untie the wisdom knot'.

odon-nyera-fie-kwan.name: Odo Nyera Fie Kwan
odon-nyera-fie-kwan.description: 'Love never loses its way home' — symbol of the power and constancy of love to find its way back.
odon-nyera-fie-kwan.proverb: Odo nyera fie kwan — 'love never loses the road home'.

okodee-mwowere.name: Okodee Mmowere
okodee-mwowere.description: 'Talons of the eagle' — symbol of strength, bravery and power. The eagle is one of the mightiest birds in Akan lore.
okodee-mwowere.proverb: The eagle's talons are the measure of its strength.

onyankopon-adom-nti-biribiara-beye-yie.name: Onyankopon Adom Nti Biribiara Beye Yie
onyankopon-adom-nti-biribiara-beye-yie.description: 'By God's grace, all will be well' — symbol of hope, providence and faith that whatever the circumstance, God's mercy sees us through.
onyankopon-adom-nti-biribiara-beye-yie.proverb: Onyankopon adom nti biribiara beye yie — 'by God's grace, all shall be well'.

osram-ne-nsoromma.name: Osram Ne Nsoromma
osram-ne-nsoromma.description: 'The moon and the star' — symbol of love, faithfulness and harmony. As the star waits for the moon, lovers remain faithful to one another.
osram-ne-nsoromma.proverb: Kyekye pe aware — 'the north star has a deep love for marriage; she is always in the sky awaiting the return of the moon'.

owo-foro-adobe.name: Owo Foro Adobe
owo-foro-adobe.description: 'Snake climbing the raffia tree' — symbol of steadfastness, prudence and diligence in undertaking a difficult task.
owo-foro-adobe.proverb: To climb the raffia tree, even the snake must plan.

owuo-atwedee.name: Owuo Atwedee
owuo-atwedee.description: 'The ladder of death' — symbol of mortality. 'Everyone will climb the ladder of death' — all must reckon with their end.
owuo-atwedee.proverb: Owuo atwedee, obaakofo mforo — 'the ladder of death is not climbed by only one person'.

pempamsie.name: Pempamsie
pempamsie.description: 'Sew in readiness' — symbol of steadfastness, hardness and readiness. A people prepared are a people unshaken.
pempamsie.proverb: Pempamsie — 'that which is sewn is ready'.

sankofa.name: Sankofa
sankofa.description: 'Go back and fetch it' — symbol of the wisdom of learning from the past to build for the future. 'It is not wrong to go back for what you have forgotten.'
sankofa.proverb: Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi — 'it is not a taboo to go back and retrieve what you have forgotten'.

sankofa1.name: Sankofa (heart variant)
sankofa1.description: Alternate, heart-shaped variant of Sankofa. Same meaning: return and retrieve what was lost; draw on the past to inform the future.
sankofa1.proverb: Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi — 'it is not wrong to go back for what you have forgotten'.

sesa-wo-suban.name: Sesa Wo Suban
sesa-wo-suban.description: 'Change or transform your character' — symbol of life transformation. One is not bound to the ways of the past; character can be remade.

tamfo-bebre.name: Tamfo Bebre
tamfo-bebre.description: 'The enemy will stew in his own juice' — symbol against jealousy and envy. The ill-wisher is ultimately consumed by their own malice.
tamfo-bebre.proverb: Tamfo bebre — 'the envious one will suffer'.

wawa-aba.name: Wawa Aba
wawa-aba.description: 'Seed of the wawa tree' — symbol of hardiness, toughness and perseverance. The wawa seed is extremely hard to crack.
wawa-aba.proverb: He who is as tough as the wawa seed endures.

wo-sa-da-mu-a.name: Wo Sa Da Mu A
wo-sa-da-mu-a.description: 'If you dance to the song in the middle' — symbol of accepting consequences of one's actions and the way life's rhythms require us to move with them.
wo-sa-da-mu-a.proverb: To dance in the middle, you must know the song.

woforo-dua-pa-a.name: Woforo Dua Pa A
woforo-dua-pa-a.description: 'When you climb a good tree' — symbol of encouragement and mutual support. When you work for a good cause, others will push you up.
woforo-dua-pa-a.proverb: Woforo dua pa a, na yepia wo — 'when you climb a good tree, you are given a push'.
